hints.title: Conflict Resolution Choice Obstacle
hints.text: When intervals conflict, removing one interval resolves the overlap. Which interval should be removed to leave the maximum remaining room for future non-overlapping intervals?

hints.title: Earliest Finish Time Invariant
hints.text: Sorting intervals by end time ensures that greedily keeping the interval that finishes earliest minimizes conflicts with all subsequent intervals.

hints.title: End-Time Sorting Greedy Scan Procedure
hints.text: If intervals is empty, return 0. Sort intervals by their end times. Maintain the end time of the last accepted interval and a removal counter. For each interval, if its start time is strictly less than the last accepted end time, increment the removal counter. Otherwise, update the accepted end time to the current interval's end. Return the removal counter.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Sorting intervals by end time takes O(N log N); linear greedy scan takes O(N).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all subsets of intervals to find the largest mutually compatible subset takes exponential O(2^N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Interval scheduling theorem proves greedily picking the earliest finish time yields the optimal answer in O(1) extra space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sorting by end time rather than start time, recognizing strict inequality requirement for overlap (touching endpoints do not overlap).

solutions.approach: Greedy Interval Scheduling by End Time
